text:
AcmeApp-SRE: Hey team — after rotating our API key yesterday some calls to Redwood are 403ing, but a few clients still succeed. Happens intermittently. Trace: https://acme.inc/log/abc
maya: Thanks — can you paste a failing curl and the successful one (headers redacted) so we can compare?
AcmeApp-SRE: failing:
```
curl -i -H "x-api-key: pk_live_rotated_abc123" https://api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/2 403
{ "error": "invalid_api_key" }
```
successful:
```
curl -i -H "x-api-key: pk_live_rotated_abc123" https://eu.api.redwood.ai/v1/generate
HTTP/2 200
```
li: interesting — same key string used in both, but different endpoints. Are you behind a CDN/proxy for the eu region? Could be edge cache holding old key->account mapping.
sam: also check if any clients are using cached file-based tokens or old SDK pinned to an API key lookup cache. What do `env | grep API_KEY` show in the failing app?
AcmeApp-SRE: For the failing service (lambda), env shows:
```
API_KEY=pk_live_rotated_abc123
```
We rotate keys via vault kv, pop them into k8s secrets for pods, and copy to Lambda via secret manager. The Lambda's logs show 403s with header: `x-rw-account: acct_55` on failing requests, but successful requests show `x-rw-account: acct_77` (different customer tenant). Could be header contamination.
maya: whoops — that header is client-sent only for multi-tenant routing. If an old proxy injects stale x-rw-account, Redwood will reject the key/account mismatch. Any sidecars or API gateways that add tenant headers?
AcmeApp-SRE: We have an nginx sidecar in front of the lambda (edge EKS) that rewrites headers for internal routing. We recently rolled the sidecar but didn't restart some old nodes.
li: repro idea: hit the failing host with `curl -I -H "x-api-key: <key>"` and `curl -I -H "x-api-key: <key>" -H "x-rw-account: acct_77"` to see if header affects routing. Also check `kubectl get pods -o=jsonpath='{.items[*].spec.containers[*].env}'` on the old nodes for stale env injection.
sam: FYI vault-agent can write both `api_key` and `rw_account` secrets into the same file if templated. If someone accidentally templated account into header variable, sidecar could pick it up.
vault-agent-bot: detected recent KV put at secret/data/acme/apikey at 3067600000 by `deploy-bot` (ttl 24h). Template `rw_account={{..data.account}}` matched.
AcmeApp-SRE: Reproduced locally — when nginx adds `x-rw-account: acct_77` we get 200; without that header we get 403 on the eu host. In failing env the sidecar was adding `x-rw-account: acct_55` (old value). Restarting the sidecar on the node fixed the requests.
maya: conclusion — rotation itself was fine, but header mismatch from an out-of-date sidecar injected an old tenant header that didn't match the new key's account binding. Root cause: staggered sidecar rollout + templated secret with stale account value persisted on some nodes.
AcmeApp-SRE: Steps we took to fix: rolled nginx sidecar daemonset to force restart, ran `kubectl delete pod --field-selector spec.nodeName=<old-node>` for three nodes, and flushed API gateway cache. All good now.
li: for future mitigation: reduce secret TTL in Vault template to avoid stale account templating, add a post-rotation step to flush gateway/edge caches, and add a small script to validate `x-rw-account` matches key account via `GET /v1/keys/inspect` (internal).
sam: added to checklist: run `kubectl rollout restart daemonset/nginx-sidecar -n acme` as post-rotation canary, and verify no explicit `x-rw-account` header is being set by clients.
AcmeApp-SRE: thanks everyone! Leaving notes in runbook and will follow up if anything else pops up. :heart:
maya: marking resolved — will close the ticket after you confirm in 24h. :white_check_mark:
